title: Ryan Reynolds’ Marvel future points to a new Deadpool ensemble
body_md:
A new report about Ryan Reynolds' professional plans has renewed interest in Deadpool's future within the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Published on November 26, 2026, the coverage points to another movie involving the character after the commercial success of Deadpool & Wolverine. However, the available information does not amount to an official announcement of a fourth standalone Deadpool installment.

The report draws on a Hollywood Reporter profile concerning Reynolds and his new publicist, Kelly Bush Novak, who also represents his wife, Blake Lively. The profile mentions another Deadpool movie among the actor's upcoming projects. That reference is significant because it suggests the character remains part of Reynolds' professional plans, but it does not identify a formal title, production schedule or release date.

Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige has previously acknowledged discussions with Reynolds about Deadpool's future. Reynolds has also indicated that he was writing a project with an ensemble format. Taken together, those comments suggest that the next opportunity to see the character could involve a group of other Marvel personalities rather than another conventional solo adventure.

The distinction matters because the first two Deadpool movies originated within the Fox-era X-Men film franchise. Deadpool & Wolverine, released in 2024, brought that history into a broader Marvel setting. As the studio prepares its next major crossover events, the question is not simply whether Reynolds will return, but what kind of story will accommodate his established interpretation of the character.

Deadpool's habit of addressing the audience and acknowledging the conventions of fictional storytelling offers a distinctive creative possibility. The character can comment on continuity changes that other protagonists might not recognize. The source article suggests that this quality could make him particularly useful in stories involving changes to Marvel's fictional universe. That suggestion is editorial analysis, however, and should not be confused with a confirmed synopsis of the next project.

An ensemble approach could also allow Reynolds to retain the character's established personality while interacting with unfamiliar heroes. Whether Marvel chooses that direction, continues the existing series or adopts another format remains to be seen. No specific supporting cast or director has been established in the available report.

Avengers: Doomsday is scheduled to reach theaters on December 18, 2026, while Deadpool & Wolverine is available on Disney+. For now, the strongest conclusion is that Reynolds' relationship with Deadpool appears to be continuing. Fans awaiting a formally announced Deadpool 4 will still need confirmation of the project's title, format and production plans from Marvel.
excerpt: A new report points to another Deadpool movie, but a fourth solo installment is not confirmed.
